purpose: Give every NetCoin surface one reusable visual and interaction language so future work reduces sprawl instead of creating new one-off UI patterns.
principles: Wallet-first: normal users should understand Wallet, Explorer, and Markets before secondary tools.
One primary action per page or panel.
Progressive disclosure: advanced controls are hidden until relevant.
Trust is visible: every critical surface shows freshness, source, and status.
Reuse before invention: prefer existing cards, badges, tables, drawers, timelines, and toasts.
Errors are recoverable: explain what happened, why it matters, and what to do next.

color_roles.maintenance: planned maintenance or informational system state

status_vocabulary.Healthy: The system is working normally and data is fresh.
status_vocabulary.Warning: The system works, but attention is needed or data may be stale.
status_vocabulary.Offline: The system cannot complete the requested operation right now.
status_vocabulary.Maintenance: The system is intentionally limited, paused, or being upgraded.

page_template.rule: Show where the user is and which product mode or job the page belongs to.
Use one clear noun phrase, not marketing copy.
Explain the page in one sentence.
Only one action receives primary styling. Secondary actions are quiet.
Use two to four cards max; do not turn summaries into dashboards.
Helpful context, recent items, explanations, or linked tools.
Raw JSON, diagnostics, coin control, orderbook internals, or audit detail must be collapsed by default.

interaction_rules: Irreversible actions require review, confirmation, result, and recovery states.
Danger buttons require explicit destructive wording, never vague labels like Continue.
Copy actions must confirm what was copied.
Search fields should accept addresses, txids, blocks, markets, docs, and feature names where relevant.
Local-only labels and notes must be marked local-only.
Every important page should answer: Where am I? What can I do? What should I do next?

content_rules.error_template: What happened. Why it matters. What to do next.
content_rules.success_template: What completed. What changed. Where to verify it.

accessibility_baseline: Focus rings are visible on dark backgrounds.
QR codes have text alternatives and copy fallback.
Tables provide mobile card alternatives or safe horizontal scroll.
Status color is never the only indicator.
phase_0_3_reference: Product simplification rules live in architecture/product-simplification.json and must be applied before creating new UI surfaces.

accessibility_matrix.keyboard_navigation: All primary and secondary controls must be reachable and operable by keyboard.
accessibility_matrix.screen_reader_labels: Icon-only buttons, QR codes, status chips, and charts must expose readable labels.
accessibility_matrix.focus_visible: Interactive controls must have visible focus states using the shared focus token.
accessibility_matrix.contrast: Text, placeholders, status chips, and disabled states must meet the chosen contrast baseline.
accessibility_matrix.touch_targets: Mobile/touch controls should use minimum practical target sizing and spacing.
